ADAPTATION & DIVERSITY

What survives selection?

Three restarts each evolve 24 strategies for 20 generations using shared anchor and rotating worlds. Checkpoints compete on separate selection worlds; a locked champion then faces an untouched final test.

Success ranks first, with fitness breaking ties. Crossover, adaptive mutation and immigrants preserve diversity. Final testing uses the world count selected in Findings.

See how effort allocations and population diversity change.
An evolved strategy is a candidate, not a global optimum.

RESEARCH QUESTION

Which mechanism changes the chance of achieving a goal—and under which assumptions?

Methods, equations & interpretation Read before drawing conclusions +

Worlds & goal

Each seeded world contains points with a domain, a goal piece, hidden usefulness, and fixed recognition and execution thresholds. Structured success requires one converted insight, collaborator, and resource. The alternative requires five conversions. Duplicate secured pieces are skipped in the structured goal.

Mechanisms

For effort fractions E, A, P: speed = 1.2 + E × movement gain. Signal reach = (30 + 190 × A × attraction gain) × environment reach. Encounter radius = 15 + 20 × A × attraction gain. Clarity reduces attraction of other domains; it never filters hidden usefulness.

Recognition & execution

Recognition probability = clamp(0.12 + (P^0.65 × recognition gain + learning) × domain fit / ambiguity, 0, 0.98). Domain fit is 1 in your specialty and 0.55 otherwise. Learning increases after each encounter, capped at 0.3. Execution uses a separate fixed threshold and pauses movement for its time cost. Encounters can still arrive during execution.

Mechanism removal

The eight factorial conditions switch incremental exploration, attraction, and preparedness benefits on or off for Strategy A. Removed effort is not redistributed. Baseline motion, encounter radius, and 12% recognition remain. Removing preparedness also removes learned gains. This tests incremental benefits, not the necessity of human cognition or motion.

Uncertainty

Success intervals use the 95% Wilson method (NIST). Paired differences use 2,000 seeded bootstrap resamples of world-level contrasts. Exploratory tables use pointwise intervals. Six predeclared pattern hypotheses must repeat on independent worlds with 10,000-resample bands, using Bonferroni alpha allocation across 12 bands. Coverage is approximate. Evolution adjusts its two final-test contrasts separately. Constant paired outcomes can yield degenerate intervals; those are flagged.

Selection & replication

A 20-point allocation grid is selected on exploration worlds and evaluated on a disjoint holdout block against balanced effort. Reusing the seed reuses that holdout: change the base seed for a new replication after tuning. Holdout comparison applies to the selected candidate, not all exploratory findings.

Reading effects

A removal effect is full-model success minus success without that benefit. Pair interaction is full − without X − without Y + without both, holding the third mechanism on. Positive values mean superadditivity on the probability scale in this model, not universal synergy. Median completion time excludes failures and must be read with success rate.

Limits & reproducibility

No human observations calibrate these rules. There are no causal claims about people, no p-values, and no “luck score.” JSON exports include assumptions, allocations, seed protocol, summaries, and all run outcomes; CSV includes condition parameters per row. Model version 2.0.0. Real-world research would require a study protocol, measured variables, and external validation.
